summary: Backend testing of MediCar Plus v2.1.0 - all 20 tests PASS on POST /api/calendar/fetch plus regressions (electron manifest v2.1.0, index.html Cites module, SMS campaigns, /api/ health). No blocking issues found.

minor.issue: sources_failed uses domain label (e.g. 'Google Calendar') as the 'url' field instead of the original URL. Makes it hard for the frontend to correlate a failure back to which of the 5 submitted URLs actually failed when the same provider is used twice.

Recurring events (RRULE) are not expanded — only the first occurrence's DTSTART is evaluated against the window. Weekly/monthly appointments from Doctoralia/Calendly may be missed. Consider using recurring-ical-events or icalevents package.

Timezone-aware DTSTART is converted with _fmt_date via .date() using UTC-naive comparison. An event at 23:30 local time on 15-Aug may serialize as 21:30 UTC and still be OK, but late-night edge events near midnight in DST-shifting zones could shift ±1 day. Consider converting to local tz before formatting.

Endpoint is public/unauthenticated — anyone can use it as an open iCal proxy against arbitrary URLs (SSRF risk to internal hosts). Recommend (a) restrict to allowlisted domains, (b) reject non-http(s) schemes, (c) reject private/loopback IPs, and/or (d) gate behind a valid Premium license header like /api/sms/campaigns.

action_items: (Optional) Expand RRULE recurring events in _parse_ics — many Doctoralia/Calendly feeds use RRULE for weekly slots.
(Security) Consider protecting /api/calendar/fetch against SSRF: block private IP ranges (10.*, 192.168.*, 127.*, ::1, 169.254.*, metadata IPs) and non-http(s) schemes before calling httpx.
(UX) Include the original URL (or its index in the request array) alongside the domain label in sources_failed entries so the frontend can highlight which of the 5 rows failed.
critical_code_review_comments: calendar_sync.py:106 raises HTTPException on non-200 upstream, which is then caught and pushed into sources_failed — correct pattern, but note that a real HTTPException from inside a per-URL loop won't cause a 502 response (it's caught). Consider a custom UpstreamError exception for clarity.
MAX_EVENTS_PER_CAL=500 is a good DoS guard but silently truncates. Log a warning or return a `truncated: true` flag per source so the UI can inform the user.
Response uses timezone-aware isoformat for fetched_at — good. Consider also adding a per-event `all_day: bool` flag (currently derived by frontend from empty time string, which is brittle).
Endpoint is unauthenticated; consider adding license validation consistent with the other Premium modules (SMS campaigns, notifications) since Cites is a Premium-only feature per the PRD.
